text:
On Nov. 5 against the Rangers, Simon Benoit knocked a puck away from an open net and then scored his first goal as a Flyer. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor, who wrote that he'd been critical of Benoit this season, put it simply: "saved a goal at one end, scored a goal at the other."

It was a good night in a harder season. The undrafted 28-year-old, who came over after 215 games in Toronto, plays about 14.6 minutes a night and leads with contact (32 hits in 14 games). With him on the ice at five on five, Philadelphia gets 39% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating less offense with him on than almost any other defenseman last season (bottom 3%), so that's no surprise.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains part of it: only 21% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. The surprise: 38% of his shots come off the rush. One goal won't change his role; cleaner exits would.
headline: Simon Benoit's best night as a Flyer
